policy: two instruments recorded together, neither one silenced

bloggerCounter.source: Blogger API v3 pageViews.get - the same figure Blogger's Stats page shows
bloggerCounter.whatItCounts: every page Blogger hands over: people, crawlers, AI readers, scripts and the owner's own browser

humanCount.source: Google Analytics 4 report, carried into GROWTH_LADDER.json
humanCount.whatItCounts: a browser that ran the analytics script, which needs a person looking at a screen

automationSelfRequests.note: the nightly measurement jobs read the blog through the authenticated Blogger API only, so they do not hand Blogger a page request to count

verdict.expectedNormalRatioOnSmallBlogs: 5 to 10 times, because every blog gets crawled
verdict.plainEnglish: Blogger answers 1308 pages a day while Google Analytics sees 16.4 readers a day (80 times apart). A small blog normally sits at 5 to 10 times, so the excess is machines reading the site - search engines, AI readers and checkers - not people.
verdict.whichOneIsReal: Both count honestly; only the Google number can be read as an audience, because a page a machine fetched was never seen by anyone and carried no ad
verdict.revenueEffect: none - an advert is only counted when a browser draws it, and a script that fetches the text runs no JavaScript, so the extra pages can neither earn money nor create invalid ad traffic
verdict.guard: GROWTH_LADDER.json keeps its human viewsPerDay; this file records the second instrument and never replaces the first
